Title: New partnership to improve mental health awareness
NewsSummary: Befrienders Kenya and AKU's Brain and Mind Institute to work to break the silence on suicide
NewsContent:
Befrienders Kenya and AKU's Brain and Mind Institute announced a partnership today to improve mental health awareness in Kenya. 

The partnership will see the two organisations strengthening information systems, evidence and research for mental health. 

Befrienders Kenya focuses on suicide prevention and destigmatising the issue within communities, as suicide remains an unspoken topic in Kenya and many other African countries. The group offers free emotional support to those in distress or at risk of suicide and works on sensitising the public on the issue as a way of breaking the silence. 

As an organisation run entirely by volunteers, there is a yawning gap - in research, in the monitoring, analysis and evaluation of its interventions to explore how they help prevent or reduce suicides among those most at risk of taking their own lives. BMI, as a research-based institute focusing on mental health, is well-positioned to assist. 

Speaking during the memorandum of understanding signing ceremony, Befrienders Kenya Director Merab Liyai Mulindi said, "Data collection and surveillance will help us develop the evidence-based interventions that are essential in meeting community needs." 

The two groups will work to enhance mental health awareness by implementing science-based approaches to clinical practice research and community-based support programmes, with suicide research and prevention as one of the top priorities. 

"This presents an exciting opportunity to evolve new ways of accomplishing our goals, responsibly and collectively, while addressing gaps," said BMI Founding Director Dr Zul Merali. 

BMI and Befrienders Kenya also aim to review the national suicide prevention strategy - including the Kenya Mental Health Action Plan 2021-2025 - independently as well as collaboratively, contributing insights and supporting follow-up. 

"With the mental health taskforce report in place and the national suicide prevention strategy ready to be launched, I am sure that this partnership is well-placed to make a mark on Kenya's mental health landscape," said Ms Mulindi.
